'''Kenneth Paul Bogart''' (August 6, 1943 – March 30, 2005)<ref name=dm/> was an American mathematician known for his work on [[Preference (economics)|preference structures]]<ref>{{citation
 | last = Anderson | first = Andy B.
 | date = July 1973
 | doi = 10.1080/0022250x.1973.9989824
 | issue = 1
 | journal = The Journal of Mathematical Sociology
 | pages = 69–83
 | title = The Bogart preference structures: Applications
 | volume = 3}}</ref> and for his textbook on [[combinatorics]].<ref name=ic/>
He was a professor at [[Dartmouth College]].<ref name=dm>{{Cite web|url=https://math.dartmouth.edu/publicity/general/kpbogart-life.phtml|title=Mathematics Department : Kenneth P. Bogart (1943–2005)|website=math.dartmouth.edu|access-date=2019-11-27}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Bogart was originally from [[Cincinnati]], and was a 1965 graduate of [[Marietta College]].<ref name=dm/> He earned his Ph.D. in 1968 at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. His dissertation, ''Structure Theorems for Local Noether Lattices'', was supervised by [[Robert P. Dilworth]].<ref name=mg>{{mathgenealogy|id=10409}}</ref>

He joined the faculty of the Dartmouth College mathematics department in 1968, was promoted to full professor in 1980, and was chair of the department from 1989 to 1995.<ref name=dm/> While at Dartmouth, he supervised 17 doctoral students,<ref name=mg/> and was also active in the mentorship of freshman women in research projects in mathematics, including [[Tara S. Holm]], later to become a professional mathematician.<ref name=dm/>

==Textbook==
Bogart was the author of the textbook ''Introductory Combinatorics'' (Pitman, 1983; 3rd ed., Academic Press, 2000).<ref name=ic>Reviews of ''Introductory Combinatorics'':
*{{citation|first=M.|last=Aigner|title=none|journal=zbMATH|language=German|zbl=0545.05001}}
*{{citation|last=Alspach|first=Brian|date=June 1985|doi=10.1137/1027068|issue=2|journal=SIAM Review|pages=258–259|title=none|volume=27}}
*{{citation|last=Johnson|first=Rubin|doi=10.1002/net.3230160210|issue=2|journal=Networks|pages=237|title=none|volume=16|year=1986}}
*{{citation|title=Review of 3rd ed.|first=Arthur T.|last=White|journal=zbMATH|zbl=0956.05001}}</ref>
